sampler_rng.mechanism_observed: mx.random.state is a per-thread list object (main id != worker id). mlx_lm.sample_utils.categorical_sampling is mx.compile'd with inputs/outputs=mx.random.state captured at import. mlx_lm.server samples on its generation Thread and calls mx.random.seed(args.seed) there.

On one long-lived worker thread (server shape) the compiled sampler returned the same token for every draw and every seed (12654 x12 for 42/31415/27182); the uncompiled call on the same thread varied per seed and advanced.
sampler_rng.stock_server: server-run2-stock, server-run3-stock: fixed high-entropy prompts, t=0.7 and t=1.0, upstream 18190 and proxy 18191: 1 distinct output over 3 seeds in every group, seed-omitted (batch path) also 1 distinct over 3. sampler_rng.intervention: patched_server.py replaces only categorical_sampling with an uncompiled mx.random.categorical(logits/temp) call. server-run4-patched: words prompt 3/3 distinct over seeds at both temperatures, number prompt 2/3, seed 42 repeat identical in all 8 groups, seed-omitted 2-3 distinct.
sampler_rng.conclusion: With temperature>0, mlx_lm 0.31.3 server ignores the per-request seed and does not advance the RNG key per token; seeded outputs are deterministic functions of temperature, not stochastic samples. Exact MLX compile-trace internals are not claimed beyond these observations.
